title: Level selector screen (becomes the new main scene)
description:
Add a player-facing LEVEL SELECTOR screen that lists the real playable levels and loads the chosen one. This becomes the new run/main_scene in project.godot (so the game boots into the selector instead of straight into sector_02).

Scope (decided with the human: "pick existing levels", no lock/progress state yet):
- New scene scenes/level_select.tscn (+ scripts/ui/level_select.gd) — a CanvasLayer/Control menu following the existing HUD UI conventions (no global theme/font exists; mirror the inline Color language used in scripts/ui/player_hud.gd; VBoxContainer of buttons, MarginContainer padding). One entry per real level: Sector 01, Sector 02, and (once it exists) the new fast shmup level (TASK for that is separate; wire it in when present — until then list the two sectors).
- Selecting an entry loads that level via get_tree().change_scene_to_file(<level_path>). There is currently NO scene-change code anywhere in the project, so this introduces the first scene-transition path; keep the level path list as a single data-driven array (path + display name) so adding levels later is one line.
- Set project.godot run/main_scene to res://scenes/level_select.tscn (exactly that one line changes for the boot scene).
- Keyboard/gamepad navigable (focus the first button on ready; the project already maps move/confirm-style inputs — reuse existing actions, do NOT add new input-map actions without flagging).
- Each listed level must still be launchable directly in the editor (the selector is additive; it does not change how levels instance the player/HUD).

Tests-first (GUT, model scene-structure tests on the existing sector_02 structure tests): assert the selector scene loads headless clean; assert the data-driven level list contains the expected real level paths and that each listed path resolves to an existing .tscn (ResourceLoader.exists); assert the menu builds one button per entry. (Pure/headless assertions — do NOT attempt to assert an actual change_scene visual transition under GUT.) Keep collision/gameplay untouched (this is UI + boot wiring only).

Note: this is logic/navigation (boot scene + scene loading), so it runs full ceremony (developer tests-first -> reviewer -> PR -> CI), not a direct visual tweak.
acceptance_criteria: A level-selector scene exists (scenes/level_select.tscn) and is set as project.godot run/main_scene, so the game boots into it.

The selector lists the real playable levels (Sector 01, Sector 02; the new shmup level is added when it exists) from a single data-driven array of {path, name}; selecting one loads it via change_scene_to_file and each listed path resolves to an existing .tscn.
The menu is keyboard/gamepad navigable (first entry focused on ready) using existing input actions; no new input-map actions added without being flagged in review.
Each level remains directly launchable in the editor; player/HUD instancing per level is unchanged; no collision/gameplay logic touched.
GUT tests assert the selector loads headless clean, that the level list resolves to existing scenes, and that one button is built per entry. Full GUT suite green, gdlint clean.
